extracted.intended_audience: early-career NIH grant applicants / PD/PIs preparing K-type or other NIH grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing the mentorship, facilities/resources, biosketch, and senior/key person profile sections of an NIH K/R-type grant application, demonstrating adequate mentorship, institutional support, data/collaboration resources, and required biographical documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship (importance and plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Medicine and Division of Infectious Diseases place a high importance on mentorship of young investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe a strong relationship with a primary mentor and co-mentors, include frequency of meetings and how mentors' complementary skills will improve chances for success as an independent investigator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary mentor qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary mentor should be a skilled clinical investigator with relevant subject-matter expertise and a history of directing relevant research units and mentoring successful awardees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specific mentor accomplishments (e.g., directed relevant units, PI roles in consortia/trials, history of mentoring fellows who received K and R awards, current mentoring grants such as a K24) to document mentor's capacity to support the candidate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-mentor qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-mentors should bring complementary, interdisciplinary expertise (e.g., health policy methodology, spatial econometrics) with relevant funded research and mentoring experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document co-mentor's research focus, leadership of methodology groups, prior NIH/R01 and foundation-funded projects, and prior mentoring through T- and K-mechanisms to demonstrate value to candidate's training plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring committee composition
rubrics_metrics.description: A mentoring committee composed of experienced and successful investigators providing expertise across health policy, epidemiology, biostatistics, and large cohort experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List committee members and their roles/expertise (health policy experts, epidemiologists, biostatisticians, cohort representatives) and explain how this collective expertise will provide mentoring, advice in study design, and career development specifically relevant to the application's aims (e.g., HIV quality of care, spatial statistics, disease outcomes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship meeting frequency and interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular, documented interactions between candidate and primary mentor (example: 'standing weekly meetings' maintained over two years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of ongoing, frequent meetings and mentorship interactions (e.g., standing weekly meetings) to show sustained mentor involvement in the trainee's development and project oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Facilities & Other Resources (office, admin, software)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of candidate's private office, administrative support, grants management support, access to printers/copiers/fax and software packages (Adobe Acrobat, Microsoft Office, STATA, STAT Transfer, Reference Manager).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document available physical space, administrative and IT support, and commonly used software to demonstrate the institution can support day-to-day research and project administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference / meeting facilities and communication capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of a multifunctional conference room configurable for 35-40 people, equipped with wired/wireless internet, TV/VCR/DVD, projection screen, dry erase board, overhead projector, and state-of-the-art videoconferencing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate ability to host meetings, trainings, and remote collaboration (e.g., videoconferencing with collaborators within consortia) as part of the resources supporting the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative cohort membership & consortium involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion in large, established cohort collaborations (e.g., NA-ACCORD with >125,000 patients; IeDEA network ~250,000 subjects) that combine cohorts, specimen repositories, and harmonized data to address research questions not answerable by smaller cohorts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe consortia goals (e.g., address failure of HAART, rare events, develop novel methods), organizational cores (Administrative Core, Data Management Core, Epidemiology/Biostatistics Core), and working groups to show access to data, oversight, and collaborative structures that enable high-impact research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management Core (DMC) functions and data quality procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: DMC provides informatics expertise to merge heterogeneous data, does not maintain a centralized database but abstracts data per approved concept sheets; monitoring includes systematic review of medical records, event-driven audits, and verification of random samples of clinical events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain processes for data inclusion, central data mapping, variable definitions, quality monitoring and audits to demonstrate rigorous data governance and high-quality pooled datasets for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epidemiology/Biostatistics Core (EBC) analytic support
rubrics_metrics.description: EBC includes leaders in cohort studies who develop innovative biostatistical and epidemiological methodologies and who receive databases from the DMC for statistical analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document access to expert biostatisticians/methodologists, validated analysis approaches, and established workflows for receiving cleaned data and performing advanced analyses to support the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational resources, servers, and software availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed EBC computing system: dedicated Sun Fire E2900 server, multiple PC servers, high-end dual-socket Windows PC with many cores and large RAM, individual PCs and MacBooks; installed packages include SAS, R/Splus, and STATA; collection of routines, primers, sample and validated sample code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide hardware specs, software lists, and availability of validated code/scripting resources to show capacity for handling large datasets and complex statistical analyses; emphasize multiplatform configurations that meet future data management and modeling demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: High Performance Computing (ACCRE) availability and support
rubrics_metrics.description: ACCRE cluster with >4,000 processor cores, nodes with 3–16 GB memory each, 48 nodes with 4x Nvidia GPUs, GPFS filesystem with >325 TB usable disk space, Moab/Torque scheduling, advanced reservation system, daily backups, and 24/7/365 support with high uptime (>95%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document access to HPC resources (GPU nodes, parallel file systems, scheduling and reservation systems, backup and uptime statistics, administrative support) to justify ability to perform large-scale computing, parallel analyses, and to ensure operational reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment and software details for data management and web-based systems
rubrics_metrics.description: PC database software (MS Access, SQL Server 2005), ASP, XML, Visual Studio, JavaScript used to develop web-based data management systems; printers (various LaserJets) to support output needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the specific database and web-development stack, supported printers/formats, and other equipment to show capacity for building and maintaining data collection and management systems required by the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sections (A. Personal Statement; Education/Training with institution, degree, completion date, field; Contributions to Science; Positions and Honors) following NIH biosketch format and keep each biosketch ≤5 pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: RESEARCH & RELATED Senior/Key Person Profile required fields and attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) form requires fields such as name, position/title, organization, project role (e.g., PD/PI), degree type/year, contact info, and attachments (Biographical Sketch, Current & Pending Support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all profile fields, supply required attachments (biosketch files, current & pending support files), include tracking numbers and funding opportunity identifiers (e.g., Funding Opportunity Number: PA-16-190), and ensure roles and categories (mentor/co-mentor/advisor) are specified to satisfy application requirements.
